stem: According to the excerpt above, the Gadsden Purchase was intended to —

options.label: F
options.text: support settlement of U.S. territory gained through the U.S.-Mexican War

options.label: G
options.text: encourage commerce among U.S. states formed from the Louisiana Purchase

options.label: H
options.text: allow the United States and Mexico to share railroad construction costs

options.label: J
options.text: encourage the sale of U.S. government land in Florida

visual_elements: U.S. Secretary of War Jefferson Davis had sent Gadsden to negotiate with Santa Anna for the land. Davis valued it, as others did, as the perfect tract for the construction of the southern transcontinental railroad. The railroad line would connect western territories to the east and north, greatly increasing the accessibility of these new lands.  —"America's Story," Library of Congress, http://www.loc.gov (accessed November 12, 2009)
